title: Agentic Postgres host manifest
description: Non-secret configuration for one deployment host. Separate from project configuration on purpose: a host is shared by projects, and folding host facts into project.yaml would make a project manifest un-portable and would make the deterministic render depend on where it happened to run. additionalProperties is false at every level. This file never contains a credential; docs/decisions/0008-sensitive-key-policy.md is applied to it by the loader.

schema_version.description: Version 2 added `database_access` (Session 4). The enum is a single value rather than a list of accepted ones on purpose: a reader that predates version 2 rejects a version 2 document instead of parsing it and silently ignoring the section that says which ports may be published, and a reader at version 2 rejects a version 1 document instead of allocating ports inside a range nobody declared. Both directions fail closed.

id.description: Stable host identifier. Also the confirmation token for edge.sh promote-acme, so it is deliberately short and typeable.

supported_os_releases.description: Releases this host is permitted to run. The enum is the implementation's fixed allowlist; a manifest may narrow it but can never widen it, which is what stops an unsupported release being enabled through configuration.

public_interface.description: 'auto' resolves the interface carrying the default route. A literal name is accepted when resolution is ambiguous; the host script refuses ambiguity rather than guessing.

address_mode.description: 'direct' means the public address is assigned to this host. 'nat' means a provider forwards it, so local assignment is not expected and external reachability is proven instead.

expected_public_ipv6.description: Null unless IPv6 ingress genuinely works. A published AAAA record with broken IPv6 routing is worse than no AAAA record, so the semantic layer requires this to be set whenever a project domain has an AAAA record.

port.description: May not be 80 or 443: those belong to Traefik, and a collision would be discovered by losing either SSH or ingress.

operator_user.description: Must exist and hold at least one authorized key before hardening. Never root.

allowed_source_cidrs.description: Required and non-empty even when the value is 0.0.0.0/0. An operator with no static address must write that choice down rather than omit the field; provision-host.sh reports it as a deviation on every run.

allow_local_forwarding.description: Session 4 tunnels the direct database endpoint over SSH local forwarding. Setting this false forecloses that without an ADR.

acme_email.description: Non-secret host configuration: the ACME account contact.

initial_acme_environment.description: Const, not an enum. Production is never selected from source; it is reached only through edge.sh promote-acme, which writes root-owned edge state. This is what prevents an editing mistake from spending a Let's Encrypt production rate limit.

infisical.description: Provider coordinates only. No credential: the control-plane credential is a root-owned file named on the command line by path, and the per-project runtime credential is written by bootstrap under /etc/agentic-postgres/credentials/.

api_url.description: HTTPS only, and no userinfo component, so a credential cannot be smuggled into the URL.

organization_id.description: The organization UUID, which is what every create call actually takes. Carried alongside the slug rather than resolved from it: a slug lookup is one more API call that can fail, and it can silently resolve to a different organization if the slug is reused. The slug stays because it is what a human recognises in an error message.

runtime_folder.description: The literal folder may be identical across projects. Isolation comes from the full (project_id, environment_slug, runtime_folder) tuple, not from distinct folder strings.

database_access.description: Where this host may publish database transports, and the range it may allocate from (ADR 0040, ADR 0042). Host-level rather than per-project because a port range is a property of the machine: two projects cannot each declare their own without one of them being wrong.

loopback_address.description: The address every project publication binds. Constrained to loopback by the pattern, so `0.0.0.0` is a schema failure rather than an operator decision. This is the schema half of ADR 0040; the model and the live host are checked separately, because a value that is right in a file and wrong in a running container is the case that matters.

osRelease.description: The fixed supported-host allowlist. 26.04 is canonical; 24.04 is the documented fallback for providers that do not yet offer the canonical image, and its use is recorded in evidence.

cidr.description: Shape only. The semantic layer parses it with Python's ipaddress module, which is the thing that actually decides validity.

loopbackAddress.description: 127.0.0.0/8 or ::1, and nothing else. Written as a pattern rather than checked only in code because a host manifest is read by more than one program, and the one that forgets to check is the one that publishes.

allocatablePort.description: Unprivileged ports only. The range must also avoid the listeners this host already has; that is a relation between values and is checked by the loader, not here.
